## reference · AI optimized alternative pages guide
* AI engines prioritize objective comparison pages over branded homepages for search queries.
* Structure alternative pages with feature matrices and balanced pros and cons lists.
* Maintain neutrality to build content trust and increase chances of AI citation.
* Treat comparison pages as machine-readable data sources for LLM synthesis.
* Use a feature matrix, a balanced pros/cons list, and a "Best For" summary on alternative pages.
* Present competitor features with the same level of care as your own to build trust.
* Avoid adjectives like "unparalleled," "industry-leading," and "the best" to prevent bias filters.
* Use Schema markup to explicitly define features, pricing, and ratings.
* Use `Product` schema and `Table` markup to present comparison data in a machine-readable format.
* Prioritize speed-to-market to claim the "first-source" advantage.
* Hunt for high-intent keywords with commercial investigation intent.
* Find the intersection of high search volume and low-quality results to dominate AI summaries.
* Avoid mixing up "X vs Y" and "Alternatives to X" pages, as they serve different intents.
* Use objective tone and include structured data to increase citation rate.
* Aim for 1,200 to 1,800 words of high-utility content on comparison pages.
* Include a feature comparison table, cite third-party reviews, and include a "Best for [Use Case]" section.
* AI traffic often converts better than Google search traffic due to pre-qualified users.
* Focus on density, not length, and put information in tables when possible.
